À + a time = see you then: à demain, à ce soir, à plus tard. Matin = morning.

phrases.en: Did you have a good day?
phrases.fr: Tu as passé une bonne journée ?
phrases.ph: tew a pa-say ewn bon zhoor-nay
phrases.note: Passer une journée = to spend a day. Une journée is the day as something you live through; un jour is more like a date.
Mettre means 'to put on' for clothes, so no word for 'on' is needed. Un pyjama is singular, unlike English pyjamas.
Se mettre au lit = to get into bed. In a command, toi goes after the verb with a hyphen: mets-toi.
Le réveil = alarm clock, from se réveiller (to wake up). Mettre son réveil = to set your alarm.
Laisser = to leave something somewhere. Don't mix it up with partir, which is to leave a place.

phrases.fr: Dix minutes, et après on éteint.
phrases.note: On éteint = lights out, literally 'we switch off'. Et après = and after that, the everyday 'then'.
Prêt has no e here because it describes tout (everything), not the person being asked.

phrases.en: Do you want a hot chocolate?
phrases.note: Chaud = hot — on French taps, C stands for chaud, so it's the hot one! The describing word comes after the noun.

phrases.en: Keep the noise down, people are sleeping.
phrases.fr: Fais moins de bruit, il y a des gens qui dorment.
phrases.ph: feh mwan duh brwee, eel-ya day zhahn kee dorm
phrases.note: Moins de bruit = less noise. Il y a des gens qui dorment = there are people who are sleeping.
Literally 'make beautiful dreams'. Des turns into de when the describing word comes before the noun: de beaux rêves.
Te shortens to t' before a vowel. Careful: je t'aime bien only means 'I like you'.
For a slangier 'I'm shattered', say je suis crevée. A boy drops the final e: fatigué, crevé.
Je vais + verb = I'm going to. In se coucher, the se changes to me to match je.
Ne ... pas wraps around the verb: je ne suis pas. In quick speech the ne often disappears.

phrases.en: I'm not going to bed yet.
phrases.fr: Je ne vais pas encore me coucher.
phrases.ph: zhuh nuh veh pa-zahn-kor muh koo-shay
phrases.note: Pas encore = not yet. It wraps around vais, and me coucher comes at the end.
Si here means 'that' or 'so', not 'if'. Il est tard = it's late.
Encore + an amount = that much more: encore cinq minutes, encore un peu. Perfect for stalling!
Finir = to finish; the s in je finis is silent. Juste works like English 'just'.
French 'takes' a shower: prendre une douche. D'abord = first, and it happily sits at the end.
Il est où ... ? is the everyday 'where's ...?'. Il because chargeur is masculine; a feminine thing gets elle est où.
Vu comes from voir (to see). Pyjama is singular in French, so it's mon, not mes.

phrases.en: Can you turn the light off?
phrases.note: Tu peux ... ? = Can you ...? Follow it with the full verb, like éteindre (to switch off).
Fermer = to close, ouvrir = to open. As a command, tu fermes loses its s: ferme.
Ouverte ends in e because la porte is feminine; with a masculine word it's ouvert.
Bonne, not bon, because la nuit is feminine. Add a name to make it warmer: Bonne nuit, Maman.
Literally 'until tomorrow'. Swap in any time: à lundi, à plus tard, à tout à l'heure.
Je n'arrive pas à = I can't manage to. It sounds more natural here than je ne peux pas dormir.
French 'makes' a nightmare: faire un cauchemar. Dreams work the same way: faire un rêve.

phrases.en: Can you wake me up at seven?
phrases.fr: Tu peux me réveiller à sept heures ?
phrases.ph: tew puh muh ray-vay-yay a set ur
phrases.note: Réveiller = to wake someone else; se réveiller = to wake up yourself. Me (me) goes before the verb.
Mis is the past form of mettre (to put). Un réveil is an alarm clock; une alarme is more like a burglar alarm.
Said to one parent. If both are there, switch to dormez bien. The s in dors is silent.

phrases.en: Can I read for a bit?
phrases.note: Un peu = a bit or a little. Lire (to read) comes straight after je peux.

phrases.en: Can Monty sleep in my room?
phrases.fr: Monty peut dormir dans ma chambre ?
phrases.ph: mohn-tee puh dor-meer dahn ma shahnbr
phrases.note: Une chambre is specifically a bedroom; any other room in the house is une pièce.

phrases.en: I'm cold, can I have another blanket?
phrases.fr: J'ai froid, je peux avoir une autre couverture ?
phrases.ph: zhay frwa, zhuh puh a-vwar ew-noh-truh koo-vehr-tewr
phrases.note: French says 'I have cold': j'ai froid, never je suis froid. Une couverture = a blanket.

phrases.en: What time do I have to get up?
phrases.fr: Je dois me lever à quelle heure ?
phrases.ph: zhuh dwa muh luh-vay a ke-lur
phrases.note: Se lever = to get up, literally 'to lift yourself'. The se becomes me to match je.
